details.appearance: A Toad with a colorful Feywild aura, a scar from the Estragon Island escape, and a third multi-dimensional sensory eye that opens on command. His exact origin is disputed because another Dan exists.
details.trait: I apologize to the room first. Then I test the window.
details.ideal: Continuity. If the planes insist I am the wrong Dan, I will remain myself anyway.
details.bond: The party that keeps finding me across mazes, estates, and collapsing realities.
details.flaw: I trust the nearest exit more than the person explaining why it is locked.
details.eyes: Two ordinary eyes and one Feyward sensory eye
details.faith: Unresolved; has encountered forces that call themselves gods
details.skin: Toad green with Feywild color shift

languages.custom: Can recognize Feyward planar terminology; speaks under pressure with uncertain confidence.

weaponProf.custom: Simple weapons, short sword, improvised weapons

biography.value:
Feyward Dan — Player Character Dossier

Level 3 Feywild Adept / Dimensional Escapee. This is the parallel Feyward Dan, not the original Dan who led the Liberated Toads and lost his arm to the corrupted mage staff. Feyward Dan woke in a yellow bed at Prismari's school, survived goblin betrayal, escaped through a window, was dragged through the Mazebound, slept through multiple dimensional emergencies, and opened his third sensory eye during the Imp Ambush.

Ledger: 1,960 XP, 11 entries, Level 3, Power 5 Mortal. The actor is a playable translation of the lore; the XP ledger remains authoritative.

How to play Feyward Dan

Use charm, improvisation, and sensory magic before force. Dan is not a polished wizard. He is a displaced player character who survives by testing doors, apologizing, fleeing when necessary, and returning when the party needs his eye.
biography.public: Feyward Dan is a parallel Toad with a colorful Feywild aura, an unreliable itinerary, and one extra eye that sees what invisible enemies hoped would remain unseen.

description.value: A custom player-facing class translation for Feyward Dan. Treat as a Charisma-based half-chaotic caster with scouting and escape features. The build reflects colorful Feywild aura, unstable magic, and the sensory eye; it does not claim the lore uses a standard published class.
Medium Toad. The Feyward variant is a parallel-reality survivor. No ancestry memories are assumed to be shared with Original Dan.
Dan survived Prismari's school, a goblin ambush, the Mazebound, and multiple plane fractures. Suggested proficiencies: Insight, Persuasion, Survival, and Sylvan.

Once per short rest, open the third eye for 1 minute. You can perceive invisible creatures and identify the approximate seam of a nearby portal or planar disguise. The eye is noticeable and may attract attention.

When Dan casts a spell or crosses a planar boundary, the GM may introduce a harmless or dangerous Feyward complication: color inversion, a misplaced door, involuntary apology, or a brief duplicate shadow.

Dan is proficient with windows, thornbushes, locked rooms, and routes that were not designed as exits. Once per short rest, gain advantage on one check made to escape a confined or unfamiliar location.
Dan can recognize that his memories do not line up with another Dan. He has advantage on checks to notice identity substitution, but disadvantage when asked to prove which history is original.
A colorful aura surrounds Dan. It is visible to trained Fey creatures and may identify him as a dimensional contaminant, visitor, or valuable specimen.
Dan may reroll one failed attack or escape check per long rest, but the reroll must be described as a second attempt, not effortless competence.
Dan knows the maze took him once. He has advantage on one check per journey to notice when a route is looping, singing, or trying to remove him from the party.
A practical blade used during the Estragon Island escape and later Feyward conflicts.
A walking staff and emergency focus; not the corrupted staff belonging to Original Dan.
A field weapon for a Toad who has learned that distance is sometimes a form of diplomacy.
Travel-worn protection suitable for movement through school corridors, hedges, and unstable estates.
A colorful scarf that marks the aura without explaining it. It is useful as a disguise accent, a bandage, or a flag when the party has become separated.
A token from the magical school where Dan woke. It may identify him to Professor Prismari or to whoever arranged the goblin ambush.
A preserved splinter from the escape route. It is evidence of the fall, not a magical weapon.

Woke in a yellow bed, entered the magical school, met Professor Prismari, was betrayed into a goblin ambush, escaped through a window, fell into thornbushes, and was hunted by a Lorehold chaos mage. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
Learned that another Dan existed in the same fractured campaign and that the archive could not safely collapse their identities. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
Was dragged into the petrified maze, separated from the party, and rescued by Bowser in a tug-of-war. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
Participated in the attempt to rescue Remi, identify Guild involvement, and understand the Regulator Plane. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.

items.name: Chronicle Card — Vostolas and the Black Crystal

description.value: Went flying during the fight while the party secured one of four portal artifacts and recruited Rattles. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.

items.name: Chronicle Card — Portal Betrayal and Gardner Vote

description.value: Stayed with the party through the vote for diplomacy, the rejected enthrallment contract, and Tymnas becoming the first diplomatic target. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.

items.name: Chronicle Card — Telescope and Tennis Match

description.value: Was displaced while the party witnessed the consequences of observing realities that could not be safely repaired. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
Entered the hellhound fight late, struck hard enough to make it flee, and contributed despite not looking graceful. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
Smelled a delivery, warned Remi before she bit, and participated in the emergency faction-name analysis. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.

items.name: Chronicle Card — Imp Ambush — Eye Opened

description.value: Opened the third eye, exposed invisible imps, and called their positions to Eager and Markop. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
Active and unknown across a three-plane system. The next scene may begin with a door, a maze, or another Dan. This is a campaign reference card and does not award XP a second time.
